base_rate.reference_class: KMT winning the most of Taiwan's 22 mayor/magistrate seats: achieved in 3 of the last 4 local cycles (2018, 2022, and 2010-era equivalents); opposition party to the sitting president has won every local midterm since 2014

evidence: 2022 baseline: KMT took 13-14 of 22 seats vs DPP 5 — the KMT starts with a huge incumbency and open-seat-defense advantage.

2026-08/09 (Kharis Templeman previews): safe/likely/leans-KMT seats include Taoyuan, Keelung, Miaoli, Nantou, Changhua, Yunlin, Hualien, Kinmen, Lienchiang, Hsinchu County, Taitung (~11 before counting Taipei/New Taipei/Taichung); DPP safe/likely roughly Tainan, Kaohsiung, Pingtung, Chiayi County plus leans-DPP Yilan.

2025-11-01 (Focus Taiwan/Wikipedia): failed 2025 mass recall left KMT legislators intact; new chair Cheng Li-wun sustains KMT-TPP cooperation, which avoided vote-splitting in New Taipei (no TPP candidate) and Yilan (joint nomination).
2026-10-20 (Taipei Times): countervailing late-October DPP momentum in Taipei and New Taipei polls — losing both plus Taichung would cut KMT to ~10-11, still likely a plurality.
Tie-breaker note: in an exact tie the market resolves to the alphabetically first English name, which favors DPP — a marginal drag on KMT probability.
0xc0f076bc4d90a44df34a729277e9d1f294f0cb.strongest_opposing_case: If the October metro swing is real and uniform, the DPP could flip Taipei, New Taipei and Taichung while holding its five 2022 seats and taking Yilan, Penghu and Hsinchu City, reaching ~10-11 seats, and the alphabetical tie-breaker hands any tie to the DPP, not the KMT.
0xc0f076bc4d90a44df34a729277e9d1f294f0cb.reasoning_summary: Base rate ~0.80 for KMT plurality: midterm penalty against the ruling DPP plus the KMT's deep structural advantage in county races (11+ seats rated safe/likely/leans blue before the big-city toss-ups). Even a bad KMT night in the metros leaves ~10-12 seats vs a realistic DPP ceiling of ~9-10. Late DPP momentum and the DPP-favoring tie-breaker trim it. Final 0.88.

base_rate.reference_class: DPP nominees for Tainan mayor: DPP has won every Tainan mayoral/magistrate race since 1997, usually by double digits (2022 closest at ~5 points)

evidence: 2026 (Taiwan News): Chen Ting-fei won the DPP Tainan primary with 60.85%, defeating Lin Chun-hsien decisively — no lingering nomination dispute reported.
2026-09-07 (Focus Taiwan): registered field — Chen Ting-fei (DPP), Hsieh Lung-chieh (KMT), one minor-party and one independent candidate; incumbent Huang Wei-che term-limited.

2026-10 (Focus Taiwan campaign coverage): no public poll showing the KMT's Hsieh competitive was found through 2026-10-25; Tainan draws little national attention compared with the toss-up metros, itself a sign the race is not viewed as close.
0x3e99612283f8182aefc17bbb51087f43c42360.strongest_opposing_case: The 2022 Tainan race was unexpectedly close (~5 points) amid local corruption controversies; a strong anti-DPP midterm wave plus 2025-26 flood-recovery grievances in the south could compress Chen's margin, and Hsieh Lung-chieh is a seasoned Tainan politician.
0x3e99612283f8182aefc17bbb51087f43c42360.reasoning_summary: Base rate ~0.85 for the DPP in Tainan, its safest big city since 1997. Chen Ting-fei won the primary cleanly with over 60%, faces a KMT opponent with no polling evidence of competitiveness, and analysts rate Tainan safe/likely DPP. The 2022 near-miss and midterm wind warrant no premium above base. Final 0.85.

base_rate.source: New Taipei mayoral results 2010-2022 (CEC via Wikipedia)

evidence: 2026-09-07 (Focus Taiwan): Su Chiao-hui (DPP) registered vs Lee Shu-chuan (KMT) and one independent; no TPP candidate, removing the three-way dynamic.
2026-01-22 (Formosa e-paper): Su 32.7% vs Lee 34.2% (Huang Kuo-chang TPP 15.4%) — within 1.5 points even before the TPP exit.

2026-10-20 (Taiwan News/Taipei Times, Taipei Trust in Democracy Association): Su 43.1% vs Lee 30.0% (+13.1) — the pollster leans green, but it is the only October reading and matches its Taipei wave direction.
Context: Su Chiao-hui has represented a New Taipei constituency since 2016, ran a two-year ground campaign, and is the daughter of former premier Su Tseng-chang, who twice ran for the seat.
0x598c99fbef3a7d4fb2c3a5af62e67e4ef5f5f7.strongest_opposing_case: No DPP candidate has ever won New Taipei; Lee Shu-chuan polls exceptionally on competence from his Taipei deputy-mayor tenure, the blue vote is consolidated with no TPP spoiler, and the sole poll showing Su +13 is from a green-leaning house contradicted by January's blue-tilted near-tie.
0x598c99fbef3a7d4fb2c3a5af62e67e4ef5f5f7.reasoning_summary: Base rate ~0.35 for a DPP New Taipei win. Su was within 1.5 points of Lee in January even with a TPP candidate in the field, and the only October poll has her +13; Lee's late entry and first-time-candidate status add KMT risk. Structural KMT advantage and poll-house uncertainty keep Lee the nominal favorite. Final 0.44.
